scope: Assistant-authored synthetic development corpus, frozen before first run; no independent human annotation. Scenario relevance measures explicit use-context evidence, not general topic relevance or suitability.

documents.text: I used the apartment internet for work video meetings between 10 am and noon for a week, without disconnections.
In this unit the internet repeatedly disconnected during weekday afternoon video conferences.
During my stay I held remote meetings from 1 am to 5 am in the apartment. The connection stayed up throughout those four hours.
The apartment router restarts every night at 2 am. My overnight video meetings were interrupted by this outage.
I completed several ten-minute video calls from this apartment without losing the connection. I did not try longer calls.
Even a ten-minute video meeting from this unit disconnected twice. The internet was unreliable during my stay.
I ran four-hour video conferences from the apartment with no interruption. This report does not specify the time of day.
The connection works for short calls, but after two hours in a continuous video meeting it disconnects and needs a restart.
Apartment amenities include Wi-Fi internet access. No measured performance or meeting experience is provided.
An international conference center nearby rents rooms by the hour. This says nothing about the apartment internet.
住这套房时我凌晨开会，画面频繁卡住，最后只能改用手机流量。

label_notes: Short-good explicitly states longer calls were not tested, so it is relevant to long-call evidence limitations. Long-risk explicitly distinguishes short versus long connections. Night/full cases accept evidence about either stated context dimension, not a claim that all dimensions or cross-border performance are verified. All candidates share identical structured filters; each has one short source, isolating ranking from context-length effects.
